# Adding Pulse to PowerPoint (sideloading)

Pulse is an Office **content add-in**. PowerPoint loads it from a web address written in a small XML file, the
*manifest*. "Sideloading" means giving PowerPoint that manifest. There are two manifests, both generated by
`pnpm build` (`pnpm manifest:build`) from `apps/addin/manifest.template.xml`:

| File | Points to | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/addin/public/manifest.dev.xml` | `https://localhost:3443` | Pulse running on your own computer (local mode, `pnpm dev`) |
| `apps/addin/public/manifest.xml` | `https://{APP_DOMAIN}` or `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | Pulse on a server; also downloadable at `https://{APP_DOMAIN}/addin/manifest.xml` |

Both use the same add-in id, so **register only one of them at a time** (remove the other first, see below).

Requirements: PowerPoint desktop app on Windows (Microsoft 365 / 2021 or newer) or Mac. PowerPoint on the web is
not supported.

---

## 1. Your own computer (local mode)

`pnpm setup:local` (or the first run of `Start-Pulse.cmd` / `Start-Pulse.command`) already did everything:

1. installed and trusted a certificate for `localhost` (`office-addin-dev-certs`),
2. registered `manifest.dev.xml` (`pnpm addin:register`):
   - Windows: registry key `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Office\16.0\WEF\Developer`,
   - Mac: copy in `~/Library/Containers/com.microsoft.Powerpoint/Data/Documents/wef/`.

Then: **restart PowerPoint** → *Insert → Add-ins → My Add-ins* (newer Microsoft 365 ribbon: *Home → Add-ins →
More Add-ins → My Add-ins*) → **Developer Add-ins** → *Pulse*. Pulse must be running (`pnpm start`) whenever you
edit or present.

Useful commands:

```bash
pnpm sideload          # opens PowerPoint with Pulse registered (alternative to the menu)
pnpm addin:register    # register manifest.dev.xml again (e.g. after it changed)
pnpm addin:unregister  # remove it
```

### Phones in local mode (cloudflared quick tunnel)

Phones cannot open `https://localhost:3443` on your laptop. A quick tunnel gives your local Pulse a temporary
public HTTPS address. The easy way: start with **`Start-Pulse-Online.command`** (Mac) / **`Start-Pulse-Online.cmd`**
(Windows) or `pnpm start:online` (`scripts/online.mjs`): it finds or downloads `cloudflared` (into `.tools/`),
starts the tunnel, reads the address and starts Pulse with `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` set to it for that run (it overrides
`.env`). QR code and join strip on the slides switch to the new address as soon as the slide connects; the add-in
itself keeps loading from `localhost`.

Manual way:

1. Install cloudflared — Windows: `winget install --id Cloudflare.cloudflared`; Mac: `brew install cloudflared`.
2. With Pulse running: `cloudflared tunnel --url https://localhost:3443 --no-tls-verify`
3. Copy the printed `https://….trycloudflare.com` address into `.env` as `PUBLIC_BASE_URL=…` and restart Pulse.
   The address changes each time you start the tunnel; update `.env` again.

Quick tunnels are for testing only (no uptime guarantee, rate limits). For lectures use a server
([deployment.md](deployment.md)).

---

## 2. Pulse on a server — testers and colleagues

After deploying ([deployment.md](deployment.md)) the manifest for your domain is at
`https://{APP_DOMAIN}/addin/manifest.xml`.

### Windows: shared-folder catalog

1. Put `manifest.xml` into a network share (e.g. `\\fileserver\pulse-addin\`). Testers need read access.
2. PowerPoint: *File → Options → Trust Center → Trust Center Settings → Trusted Add-in Catalogs*.
3. Enter the share path (`\\fileserver\pulse-addin`) as *Catalog URL* → *Add catalog* → tick **Show in Menu** → OK.
4. Restart PowerPoint → *Insert → Add-ins → My Add-ins* → **Shared Folder** → *Pulse* → *Add*.

Without a network share, a single PC can use the developer registration instead:
`npx office-addin-dev-settings register path\to\manifest.xml`.

### Mac

1. Download `https://{APP_DOMAIN}/addin/manifest.xml`.
2. Copy it into `~/Library/Containers/com.microsoft.Powerpoint/Data/Documents/wef/`
   (create the `wef` folder if it does not exist; in Finder: *Go → Go to Folder…*).
3. Restart PowerPoint → *Insert → Add-ins → My Add-ins* → *Pulse*.

### Developer (any OS)

```bash
npx office-addin-debugging start apps/addin/public/manifest.dev.xml desktop --app powerpoint
```

---

## 3. Later: university-wide rollout

Microsoft 365 admin center → **Settings → Integrated apps → Upload custom apps** → *Office Add-in* → upload
`manifest.xml` → assign to a **pilot security group** first, then widen. Deployment to users can take up to
24 hours. **[VERIFY]** the menu names at the time of rollout (Microsoft renames them regularly) and note them here.

Known risk to check before the rollout: [OfficeDev/office-js#6913](https://github.com/OfficeDev/office-js/issues/6913)
— centrally deployed PowerPoint *content* add-ins did not open after a July 2026 update while sideloaded ones
worked. Test with the pilot group before announcing it.

---

## 4. Updates

- **Code updates are live immediately**: the add-in is a web page served by the Pulse server. Deploy the server,
  done — no re-sideloading.
- **Only manifest changes** (domain, name, icons, permissions) need the new `manifest.xml` to be redistributed
  (shared folder, `wef` folder or admin center). Then restart PowerPoint.

---

## 5. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| Pulse not in *My Add-ins* | Restart PowerPoint completely (Windows: check Task Manager; Mac: Cmd+Q). Windows: look in the *Developer Add-ins* or *Shared Folder* tab. Re-run `pnpm addin:register`. |
| Frame shows "We can't open this add-in from localhost" or stays white | Pulse is not running — start it. Open `https://localhost:3443` in Edge/Safari: there must be **no** certificate warning; otherwise run `pnpm certs` again (Windows: answer *Yes*; Mac: enter your password). |
| Old version keeps showing | Clear the Office web cache. Windows: close PowerPoint, delete `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Office\16.0\Wef\`. Mac: close PowerPoint, delete `~/Library/Containers/com.microsoft.Powerpoint/Data/Library/Caches/` (the `wef` folder with the manifest stays). |
| Two Pulse entries / wrong server | Both manifests are registered. `pnpm addin:unregister`, remove the other copy (shared folder / `wef`), restart PowerPoint. |
| Phones show "no connection" | The address on the slide must be reachable from mobile data: tunnel running and `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` set (local mode), or server firewall 80/443 open (server mode). |
